metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the manifest's concrete serialization format (e.g. sorted-key JSON / JSONL) and field layout so the byte-identical AC is well-defined.
evidence: The plan states 'It emits no YAML' but never states what format it DOES emit (JSON, JSONL, TSV).
The byte-identical AC and the per-candidate fields (direction, tier, signals, rank) plus zero-candidate rows imply a concrete on-disk schema the executor must choose.
findings.finding: The output artifact (the 'LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST') has no stated serialization format, yet an acceptance criterion depends on it being byte-identical across runs.
findings.location: Approach ('An offline selector writing a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST'); AC 'Two consecutive real runs ... emit a byte-identical manifest'
scenarios: Executor picks JSON with unordered keys and the byte-identical diff becomes non-deterministic despite deterministic ranking.
A downstream emitter (separate ticket) cannot parse the manifest without an agreed format.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the format explicitly (e.g. 'a JSON object with sorted keys, one candidate object per row') so the diff AC is deterministic and the emitter has a stable contract.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how a no-fire candidate obtains its (criterion, norm_id) key — e.g. state that the norm_id must have fired in at least one review carrying that material_fingerprint and 'stayed absent' means it dropped out of the other equal-fingerprint reviews — so the no-fire direction is constructible.
evidence: Plan: 'A candidate is keyed by (criterion, norm_id) (sidecar.py:656,663)'
Plan: 'Reproduction consensus — the key fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or more reviews with equal material_fingerprint. The only signal valid in the no-fire direction.'
labels.py:180-185 _criterion_sets builds norm_id sets only from findings present in a review (a norm_id exists only for a fired finding)
AC 'A key present only in equal-fingerprint pairs records reproduction consensus' still presumes the key exists
findings.finding: The no-fire reproduction-consensus direction keys candidates on (criterion, norm_id), but norm_id is derived only from a finding that actually FIRED; the plan does not specify where a no-fire candidate's norm_id comes from when the key 'stayed absent' across the equal-fingerprint reviews.
findings.location: Approach → Label signals → Reproduction consensus; and Candidate key and signal join
scenarios: A criterion that should correctly stay silent on some material but has no fired finding anywhere in the equal-fingerprint set — there is no norm_id to key the no-fire candidate on, so it can never be recorded

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Realign the leaf's no-fire signal to the parent's predicate: admit a no-fire candidate for criterion C only when C is in the cohort set of some finding on the plan (proving C was routed) AND no finding cites C, skipping missing-cohort rows — folding reproduction consensus in as a corroborating rank/tier signal on top of that gate, not as a standalone no-fire admission rule.
evidence: Leaf: 'Reproduction consensus — the key fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or more reviews with equal material_fingerprint. The only signal valid in the no-fire direction.'

Parent 65dd: 'The selector admits a plan as no-fire evidence for criterion C only when C appears in the cohort set of some finding recorded for that plan (sidecar.py:667-672, proving C was routed) AND no finding on that plan cites C; a row with a MISSING cohort key is treated as unknown and skipped...'
Parent 65dd Child decomposition: 'No-fire predicate AC -> the selector (owns/applies the cohort + no-finding predicate)'.
Parent rationale the leaf drops: 'silence from the criterion never being routed to that plan is indistinguishable from silence from finding nothing.'
The leaf plan text contains no mention of 'cohort' anywhere; its no-fire direction is grounded only in material_fingerprint absence-consensus.
findings.finding: The leaf's no-fire evidence signal (reproduction consensus over equal-material_fingerprint reviews) redefines the parent's no-fire predicate, which this selector was explicitly assigned to own. The parent admits a no-fire (expect: pass) case for criterion C only when C is in the cohort set of some finding on that plan (proving C was ROUTED) AND no finding cites C, with missing-cohort rows skipped; the leaf's no-fire direction rests on absence-consensus alone and never carries the cohort/routed-to-plan requirement, so it would admit no-fire candidates the parent's contract forbids.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Label signals' (Reproduction consensus bullet) and 'Candidate key and signal join'; vs parent 65dd 'No-fire evidence predicate' and 'Child decomposition' (No-fire predicate AC -> the selector).
scenarios: A criterion that was never routed to a plan (never in any finding's cohort on that plan) is silent across two equal-fingerprint reviews; the leaf's reproduction-consensus rule admits it as a no-fire candidate, but the parent's predicate would skip it as unknown.
A corpus row with a missing cohort key: the parent requires it be skipped as unknown; the leaf's no-fire signal has no provision to exclude it.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Label signals' / 'Candidate key and signal join' sections, add the cohort-membership + no-finding predicate (sidecar.py:667-672) as the precondition for any no-fire candidate and state that missing-cohort rows are skipped, matching parent 65dd's no-fire evidence predicate; keep reproduction consensus as the signal that raises such an admitted no-fire candidate to ADVISORY.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the vintage gate resolves rubric commit history when `origin/main` is unavailable (shallow clone, alternate remote name, server checkout) — either a defined fallback ref or an explicit hard error, so the gate never silently excludes every criterion.
evidence: Plan: 'A review is eligible for criterion C only when `review_event_ts` postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching C's rubric file.'
Plan: 'A criterion whose resolved file has no `origin/main` history ... FAILS the gate and is recorded as a zero-candidate row with reason `no-committed-prompt-history`.'
rebar must run 'from many project locations' and under 'CI under any provider' — a shallow clone or a differently-named remote makes the `origin/main` ref unresolvable.
findings.finding: The vintage gate resolves rubric history via git-log against `origin/main`, silently assuming that ref exists; in a checkout where it does not (shallow CI clone, a remote not named `origin`, or a server checkout outside the primary clone), the git-log returns no history for every criterion, so every criterion fails the gate and the manifest emits only zero-candidate `no-committed-prompt-history` rows.
findings.location: Approach → Vintage gate ('postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching C's rubric file')
scenarios: CI venue (any provider) with a shallow/single-branch clone lacking a full `origin/main` history: git-log finds no commits touching the rubric file, so every uncovered criterion is emitted as a `no-committed-prompt-history` zero-candidate row and the manifest carries zero real candidates — the user sees an empty selection with no error.
A server outside the checkout or a repo whose upstream remote is not named `origin`: the `origin/main` ref does not exist, git-log errors or returns empty, and the whole run degrades to all-excluded.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the base ref portably (e.g. the configured upstream tracking ref or a required-ref precondition that fails loudly) rather than hardcoding `origin/main`, and distinguish 'ref missing' from 'no history' so an unresolvable ref does not masquerade as `no-committed-prompt-history`.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive or measurement-justify MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 against the observed decision_margin distribution (or note it as a stated tunable default with rationale).
evidence: The plan justifies the reviewer-noise hazard with data (208/551 flips) but the specific 0.15 cutoff is stated as a constant, not derived: 'The constant drops findings close enough to block_threshold that a small perturbation flips them.'
No AC or step measures the distribution of abs(decision_margin) to justify 0.15 versus another value.
findings.finding: MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 is asserted as a constant with a rationale but no derivation from the corpus data, and there is no measurement step establishing that value.
scenarios: 0.15 admits noisy fire candidates as BLOCKING (or excludes stable ones), skewing which fixtures gate rubric edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note/step deriving 0.15 from the margin distribution over the committed corpus, or explicitly frame it as a tunable default.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the labeled-candidate-manifest schema and label-signal semantics in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc so the emitter has a documented contract.
evidence: A new module under src/rebar/llm/evals/ produces a manifest consumed by a separately-owned emitter — a new cross-component contract.
No documentation sub-check output (ADR/AGENTS.md/design doc) is mentioned for the novel manifest schema or the label-signal semantics.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new pipeline stage and inter-tool contract (selector -> labeled candidate manifest -> separate emitter/admission runner) but captures no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc record of that contract.
findings.location: Approach / Scope / Non-goals ('the emitter and admission runner own those')
scenarios: The emitter ticket implements against a different assumed manifest shape; the contract drifts with no documented source of truth.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that a git-log EXECUTION failure surfaces an error (not the 'no-committed-prompt-history' domain reason), distinguishing subprocess failure from empty history.
evidence: The plan carefully handles the DOMAIN case 'no origin/main history' as a zero-candidate row, but never distinguishes it from a git EXECUTION failure.
A git subprocess error and an empty history would both surface as 'no commits' unless disambiguated.
findings.finding: The selector shells out to git (git-log for rubric history) — an external process boundary — but the plan does not state how git invocation failures (git unavailable, subprocess error, non-zero exit) are handled versus the domain 'no history' outcome.
findings.location: Approach, 'Vintage gate' — 'git-log .rebar/prompts/<pid>.md' and 'no origin/main history ... FAILS the gate'
scenarios: git errors (detached/corrupt repo, git absent under the network guard) get silently misread as 'no-committed-prompt-history', excluding valid criteria.
